BrickKit CLI — build systems like snapping together bricks.

You declare which components you want and what they depend on; the CLI derives the rest and hands it to Docker, Podman or Kubernetes.
A project is described in three layers:
  brickkit.yaml       which components, at which exact versions
  deploy.yaml         how they are deployed (your personal deploy.local.yaml stays out of Git)
  config/             the environment variables each component gets

What the CLI does:
  1. Pull components and artifacts (Git / local directories / Market) and write them into the three layers
  2. Resolve dependencies and work out the start order (required/optional dependencies + topological sort)
  3. Generate deployment files, run migrations and call the underlying engine (compose / kubectl)
  4. Build local images and release component versions (build / release / publish)
  5. Manage the component source workspace (--repo / sync)

It is not a long-running service: it exits once the command finishes and uses no background resources.

Usage:
  brickkit
  brickkit [command]

Examples:
  brickkit init my-project              initialize a project
  brickkit add erp/backend@1.0.0        add a component (dependencies are pulled recursively)
  brickkit up --dry-run                 compute without starting: see what would run and in what order
  brickkit up                           generate deployment files and start
  brickkit status                       show the running state
  brickkit down                         stop (volumes are kept)

Project commands:
  deps        Print the dependency tree
  graph       Output the project's dependency topology as a Mermaid diagram
  init        Create a project, or complete the three-layer skeleton in the current directory
  lint        Check the three layers (brickkit.yaml, deploy files, config/) and component.yaml offline
  restore     Restore mode in deploy.yaml and the component source layout to the last commit
  skills      Show and refresh the AI assistant skills installed into the project

Component commands:
  add         Add a component, pull its dependencies and artifacts recursively, and write it into the three layers
  build       Build the component images that need a local build
  fetch       Download a component's artifacts (API contract, SDK, ...) without installing it into the project
  new         Generate the minimal skeleton of a new component
  release     Release a component version: check, tag and push to its Git repository
  remove      Remove a component: drop its entries from the three layers and archive its config in config/.archive/
  sync        Tidy the component source workspace: move source you don't need this run into .archived/
  upgrade     Upgrade a component's default version and migrate its config

Lifecycle commands:
  down        Stop every component in one go (volumes are kept)
  local       Manage deploy.local.yaml, your personal copy of deploy.yaml
  status      View the running state of components (reads the underlying engine)
  up          Generate the deployment files, run migrations and start every component in one go

Market commands:
  login       Log in to the component Market; the token is stored in .brickkit/credentials
  logout      Log out of the Market: revoke the token on the server and delete the local credentials
  publish     Publish a component to the Market (brickkit login first)

Additional Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  lang        Show the CLI's current display language
  version     Show the CLI version, the supported Manifest version and the deploy targets

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for brickkit
      --log-level string   Level of the JSON logs on stderr (debug | info | warn | error | off) (default "off")

Use "brickkit [command] --help" for more information about a command.
